# CityBuilderSim

*Build 0.7.77 · Save format 34 · 8 October 2026*

A macroeconomic city simulator: an age pyramid that decides the workforce, a labour market that prices it and in which every worker takes the best-paid post they qualify for, builders who share their crews by what each site can use and are paid at today's wages, with the player's hand on their queue to reorder it, rush it on overtime, cancel an order or pull a building down, seventeen private sectors on one template trading real goods on real markets — two of them selling to the world, one of them to the mills, one hauling the others' freight, one building the cars the households drive and two lifting the oil and cutting it into the petrol and diesel they burn and the rest of a barrel — and raising their money with shares and bonds that trade on order books and keeping accounts that read as real statements, a bank that is a business, pricing a loan from what it costs, keeping its own capital and passing to the city when it fails, a central bank whose balance sheet is the only place money is made, whose dial is the price of it, whose holdings can reach every bond the city sells and whose credibility anchors what people expect prices to do, and so the level every money constant is struck at, a city founded with a name and a money of its own on a world of its own seed — an Earth-sized square of sea, coast and lakes with seven resources lying in finite fields — buying its ground a rectangle of whole blocks at a time from six offers a side, at a price its crowding sets, drawing no more fresh water than its lakes yield, drawn on a map building by building, made to borrow for what it builds and able to build its own works a margin ahead within a debt limit, and with a fund it saves in, trades by hand and draws on at a dial, households that each keep their own books including the people the books used to leave out, illness that kills, crime that has reasons, households that eat thirteen separate foods, choose between them by income and ask for them at a price the shops clear on, with a voucher the city can pay toward them, own cars, borrow for them and buy their petrol, and spend what is left over a counter, a road that carries three kinds of traffic, is priced over its life, can be paved, and can be relieved but never deleted, beside buses the treasury pays for and riders who weigh the fare against what driving costs them, a trade band that is three quarters freight, a currency with a balance of payments behind it, a vault that spends to defend it and a real rate that moves it, and every screen drawn as pictures that open onto the figures behind them, a history among them that the player can drag, zoom and read their own decisions on. This is what it currently has and does.

## 1. The month

*Everything in the game happens in this order, and most of the hard bugs in its history have been a line that made it into one phase and not the other. The order is genuinely a sequence, so it is numbered — and since 18 September it is also generated: `docs/month-order.md` lists every top-level statement of `Game.nextMonth()` and `SimulationEngine.simulateMonth()` with its line, which is what this list is struck against.*

1. **Automatic building orders the city's works, the month's money is struck, and what falls due is rolled, before the calendar turns** — First, while the player has it on, automatic building takes its pass (`autoBuilder.pass()`, 0.7.73): between the presses, where the player's own Build lands, on the city the last press left and at the prices it was quoted, it orders the build advice's own cards for the city's works within the builders, the budget and the player's debt limit, and since 0.7.77 buys the bare ground they lack (see the screen, section 22); off, it returns at once. Then the month's money constants are struck at the price level people expect, the level the last month ended on (`expectations.strikeLevel()`, `restrikeMoneyConstants()`, 0.7.42): the shelf's floor, the land office's bases, what every building costs and its upkeep, the clinics' fees, tuition, the pension's wage base, the fare, a founding share and the bank's fees and paid-in. So the month lives at one level from here to the next press, and no constant reads a price it sets. Then what falls due is rolled, in the gap between two presses, where a player's own issue lands, so that it settles to its buyers and crosses the audit window exactly as a hand-made issue does. In a December the city's fund takes its dial's share of the year's surplus first (`fundYearEnd()`), so that no surplus is counted twice; then the rollover reads the principal that falls due next month, nets it against whatever of last year's surplus is still unused, and issues the rest, sized to the cash it has to raise (`rollMaturities()`, 0.7.13), and strikes how much of the central bank's own maturing paper it will take again at issue. Then the month turns, and as it turns the buildings the player ordered demolished between the presses close (`closeDemolished()`, 0.7.22), before anything in the month reads the city: their posts, homes and places are gone from its first count. No money moves there; it moved when the order was placed.
2. **The central bank settles with the treasury, and the promises are paid** — Before anything is priced, because the advances and the remittance are money made and destroyed and have to fall inside the audit's window. With the autopilot on — and a new game founds on it since 0.7.13 — the Taylor rule takes the dial, aimed at the player's target and, since 0.7.52, as strictly as the player holds it. Then the treasury pays the interest on last month's advances, takes last month's profit back as the remittance and the city's fund's withdrawal (by default a twelfth of 3% of all it is worth, from its cash; over the default since 0.7.48, last month's sale first), repays its central bank out of any cash above zero, pays down arrears — since 0.7.55 a line of each payee's cash flow, *Arrears paid by the city*, where the money had reached the till and no line — and is advanced whatever it is still short (`settleTreasury()`). Then the central bank takes its own maturing par again, as an add-on to what the city sold between the presses (`rollCentralBankAtIssue()`, 0.7.15), and the holdings dial trades the city's term paper toward its target (`openMarketOperation()`), so this month's quotes carry both. Then the students' grant and EI are paid on the people the month opens with, in the month they are credited, and the bank pays its profit tax.
3. **The world turns and the land office re-prices** — World prices advance, the exchange rate is taken, the cost of living goes into the labour market — since 0.7.42, once the basket is based, half of its move the inflation people expect and half a forty-eighth of the way to the index — and the land office strikes its ground in US dollars and what businesses pay for it in the city's own money, and since 0.7.67 lists any of its twenty-four places that waited for room and has it now (`LandMarket.update()`). What the city pays outside and what businesses pay inside are both inputs to everything below.
4. **Business credit is priced, interest billed, property tax charged** — What its money costs the bank goes to the city's floor first, and a failed bank lends nothing. Then the bank's capital rule is read once and handed to every desk that lends this month, the businesses' and the families', its bonds and its book's concentration re-read before it; every business's spread is set on the bank's prime at this month's dial, the landlords' insured mortgages at the insured rate beside it; and the businesses' bond coupons are struck on the same face the interest bills are, with property tax charged beside them. Before the statements run, so the figures each sector banks are net of it.
5. **Every building pays to stand, and every shipper pays its freight** — 1% of build cost a year, charged to every owner in cash *and* materials *and* construction points — placed as a real order with the builders, not a line item. Since 0.7.19 the cash is the building's cash cost with its labour at today's builders' wages, and the bill carries the builders' sales tax, which a business that makes taxable supplies claims back and the landlords and the bank bear; the city's comes back to it, since the city collects it. A forty-year stock at 1% a year is about 40% of the city's whole construction output. Then the railway's invoice on the month's trade, for the same reason: an expense on fourteen sets of books and revenue on the fifteenth.
6. **Fifteen income statements are struck** — Retail, real estate, industry, construction, heavy industry, mining, materials, business services, manufacturing, agriculture, food processing, rail, automotive, luxury retail, restaurants — each at the *utilisation the month was traded at*, not at today's, and each from the same template. The VAT is settled from the same figures between the two halves, and since 0.7.19 the sales tax a business claims back on the buildings it bought reaches its till as cash back on them. Since 0.7.44 the strike also settles the grocers' supplier credit: the till pays the month's stock bill but for what its suppliers lent against it, and repays what the strike before left owed, out of the takings of the stock that has since sold.
7. **National accounts, then the household books** — Household spending *is* consumption, read from the other end, so the people cannot be shown paying a figure the shops were not shown receiving. Consumption is three counters now — the grocers', the boutiques' and the kitchens' — plus the rent. The households' month strikes the bank's account fees, and since 0.7.19 its customers with them, which the branch rule in step 9 reads; and since 0.7.49 it charges the transit fares to the rows that ride and the month's fuel to the rows that drive. The government's part of the accounts carries the schools' and transit's costs since the same version, as step 11 struck them the month before.
8. **The households buy cars, then spend the rest over a counter** — With the month's money fresh and before the investor can see it: the second-hand market clears first, because nobody pays forty for a car they can have for twelve, then the showroom; then the boutiques, and the kitchens right after, because they are the same kind of purchase out of the same surplus. The cars, the pieces and the meals count as demand for next month's strike.
9. **The private sector takes its turn** — Loans advance; a bond that falls due is paid from its issuer's till to its holders; matured principal comes back, and a till left short calls its dollars home, sells the other sectors' bonds it holds and goes to the shortfall desk, which lends or sells a bond for it, and what it still cannot pay defaults, a slice the size of the part it cannot pay. Plant is retired and sold to the builders for its material, the bank's branches that this month's account fees no longer cover at last month's cost close (0.7.19), the month's defaults are written off against the bank, the insured part paid by the treasury, and each sector forecasts its own signal six months out, orders only what the city could staff (0.7.18), and funds what it plans in a fixed order: sell shares, spend the till, call money home from abroad, and only then borrow — a bond where one is no dearer than the loan, the bank for the rest, and a landlord's homes on an insured mortgage.
10. **Construction advances; roads recount; the builders strike their crews, the posts are counted and the labour market reprices** — The sites take the month's points by the crew each building can use (0.7.17), and once the player has a hand on the queue the city's share goes to its own sites in the player's order and a rushed site works its month on overtime (0.7.22; see the builders, section 9). The builders buy the material that work drew on and recognise revenue on the same figure the sites advanced by; each owner then pays what the month's draw cost past what its quote allowed for it, or is refunded (0.7.19), and the hand's month is settled after it — the overtime's premium paid and paid out as wages, a cancelled order's refund, a finished demolition's material and ground (0.7.22), and since 0.7.70 the gravel roads a paving replaces retired as their Paved Roads open, the ground between the two freed. A shop that opens this morning trades this month and puts its trucks on the road this month — roads are recounted before anything reads them. Then the builders strike the share of their posts the work ahead needs and lay the rest off (0.7.17), and only then are the posts recounted and wages walk toward what scarcity says per band, and per licence, against this month's posts and before anybody ages.
11. **Demographics** — Age; give birth; die of three separate causes — the band's own rate, illness, and violence; migrate, never more than the room the placement has left at the doors standing today (0.7.17); rebuild the households against last month's; commit and record this month's crime; settle health, education and the police; then the commute (0.7.49): the road is told what share of its commuters have no car of their own and what a journey's fuel costs, since 0.7.62 its litres at the price they land at (`setCommute()`, `Motoring.journeyFuel()`), the fare draws its riders, the drivers' fuel is drawn — since 0.7.62 off the refiners' tanks first and from abroad for the rest (`motoring.drawFuel()`), where it had been struck as a bill (`setFuelBill()`), and since 0.7.76 drawn as petrol — and transit's bill with it; advance the ring of the sick.
12. **The economy and the services sync** — Population, wages, jobs, the fill rate and the utilisation ratios reach every sector — the road ratio per sector, because only a tram can make two businesses on the same street face different jams, and the health ratio the demographics step has just set.
13. **Cash moves, every market clears, ore is lifted, the paper is paid, the government's books are re-struck** — The utility books what its customers were charged; every market clears and every maker produces in one pass; the mines ask the ground, and since 0.7.62 the oil wells too, each lifting what is left of the oil the city owns (`LandManager.extractOil()`), the refiners taking their crude and the railway its fuel, diesel since 0.7.76, as buyers, and since 0.7.76 a refinery shipping what its tanks cannot hold before anything could be written off. The food vouchers the sale took are paid at once, a promise in the month of the sale (0.7.43); then the tax take comes in and the promises go out a line at a time, since 0.7.49 transit's wages and upkeep among them, after the police's, where until then nobody paid them. The paper sold between the presses settles to its holders, the households taking their share first, and the month's coupons and principal are paid holder by holder. The books are re-struck at the bottom of the month, against the same period's spending and after the coupon is known, because the start-of-month call mixed two months' tax fields. Since 0.7.57 the ground's month closes with them: the forest grows back a 240th of what was cut and the month's flows of ground and ore are cleared (`landManager.endMonth()`).
14. **The bank settles, the owners are paid, the shares and the bonds trade** — The bank pays for whatever paper the households did not take and earns a month of the discount on what it holds; then lending and its fees, repayments, the interest by who paid it and its bonds' coupons, what the month asks of its allowance, its staff and its branches — the charter exempt from the operating cost since 0.7.19 — the carry trade, the window and the interest on its reserves at the central bank, and, if it has failed and the city's setting is automatic, its resolution for its shares that month; then the cost of funds is struck once and final, the central bank strikes its month's profit, the savers are paid, then dividends, then the shares trade, then the city's preferred falls due at its anniversaries, then the bonds trade, then whatever is still idle goes abroad, the households' by the same rule as the sectors', and a household whose paper no longer out-yields its deposits sells a little of it back. What lands after the bank's close can still fail it, so it is looked at again, and a bank under its minimum asks the city for preferred.
15. **The currency moves, and the money is counted** — `MoneyAudit` strikes *pooled after − pooled before = inflows − outflows* across every pool in the city and every flow across its border. A cent of residual is a finding — since 0.7.54 a cent, or a part in a trillion of what moved where that is more, because in a city of billions a double's own step passes the cent (`MoneyAudit.tolerance()`); and a comparison held to a floor of its own is never held tighter than 64 of a double's steps at the size of the figures it compares (`MoneyAudit.ULP_STEPS`; 8 in 0.7.63, 64 since 0.7.64), because an identity is a signed sum of figures that each carry their own rounding, and a floor of a millionth of a unit is under a double's step from about a billion units up. The hot money moves just before the strike, because it moves a pool; then the balance of payments, the currency and the price index, each reading a month that has finished settling, and straight after the index what people expect prices to do: credibility against the target and the lean the rate showed, expected inflation and the price level next month's constants are struck at (`expectations.takeMonth()`, 0.7.42), handed on to the investors, the currency and every sticky seller's price (`handOnExpectations()`). The index has five parts on a trailing year's spending and is chained since 0.7.43. The currency reads the real rate against the world's, ex ante since 0.7.42, and drifts at the credible part of expected inflation (`setExpectedDrift()`), and on a month it is pushed weaker on a deficit the central bank sells the vault's dollars against the push — a capital transaction booked after the audit, because no pool moves on it. Nothing after the audit may move a pool. Once the month is recorded the history folds any calendar year all of whose months have left its newest six thousand (0.7.55), and the city's map takes the month's buildings (`reconcileMap()`, 0.7.60). Every twelfth month autosaves at its very end, once the month is recorded (`recordMonth()`) — since 0.7.52; until then the file was written at the top, after the calendar turned and before anything ran, and a city loaded from it never ran that month — and the game also autosaves before any skip and on quit, both between the presses.

**What moved since the last edition.** One statement went in, at the very top, and the order of the rest held. Since 0.7.73 `Game.nextMonth()` opens with automatic building's pass (`autoBuilder.pass()`), before the money is struck, between two lines that hand a harness's watch the city before and after it and that the game never sets; off, the pass returns at once, and the default playtest, which leaves it off, wrote 0.7.72's traces to the byte. The generated list is 0.7.69's with its line numbers stripped, bar those three lines, checked by running it on both builds' sources. Inside statements that were already there, 0.7.70 has the construction step retire a paving's gravel roads as their Paved Roads open and the hand's settle free the ground between them; 0.7.74 has the month's books freeze the interest by instrument where the credit step hands the bill, and the debt by kind and by when it falls due where the sheet's debt is set; 0.7.75 has the debt's movements counted by kind where each moves and read with the sheet, and the ground and the buildings' material read at the month's prices with it; and 0.7.76 has the drivers draw petrol and the railway diesel where they drew fuel, and the refiners make the slate of their crude and ship what their tanks cannot hold. The rest — the roads over their life, childcare's sizes, the map's network and its bridges, the statements' screens, the products' prices and the split of an older save's fuel — lives in the advice, the screens, the painter and the load path. **From 0.7.65 to 0.7.69** nothing moved: no statement went in, changed or moved, and the list was 0.7.64's with its line numbers stripped. Inside a statement that was already there, 0.7.67 has the land office, as it re-prices at step 3 and after every purchase, list any of its places that waited for room and has it now; the rest of the grid — the city's ground in whole blocks, the offers six a side, the conversion of older saves at load, the units and the office's screens — lives inside the land's own methods and the load path. **From 0.7.55 to 0.7.64** one statement went in and one changed shape, at set places, and the order of the rest held. In 0.7.60 the city's map takes the month's buildings straight after the month is recorded and before the autosave (`reconcileMap()`), after the month's construction and demolitions, so the map a save writes is the month's. In 0.7.62, at 6d, the drivers' fuel struck as a bill (`motoring.setFuelBill()`) became fuel drawn as a good (`motoring.drawFuel()`), and the journey's fuel the road is told before the fare is read at the price it lands at (`Motoring.journeyFuel()`). Inside statements that were already there, 0.7.55 has the arrears the treasury pays land on each payee's statement and the record fold the history's oldest whole years; 0.7.57 has the government's books close the ground's month; 0.7.59 has the services read the fresh water limit on every path that updates them; and 0.7.62 has the markets clear crude and fuel, the wells ask the ground as the mines do, and the railway draw its fuel off the same tanks. 0.7.55 to 0.7.59, 0.7.61, 0.7.63 and 0.7.64 moved no statement: the generated list is 0.7.54's with its line numbers stripped, bar those two and the fuel the commute's statement reads. **In the editions from 0.7.23 to 0.7.54** eight statements went in, two changed shape and one moved, at set places, and the order of the rest held. Six in 0.7.42, the anchor: the month's money constants are struck at its very top, at the expected price level the last month ended on (`expectations.strikeLevel()`, `restrikeMoneyConstants()`); the currency is handed its anchored drift before it reprices (`foreign.setExpectedDrift()`); and straight after the price index the month reads the target, strikes what people expect (`expectations.takeMonth()`) and hands it on (`handOnExpectations()`). The wage step became a choice of two in the same version, half on expected inflation once the basket is based, and the index's call took its five parts in 0.7.43. Two in 0.7.49, at 6d: the road is told who has a car of their own and what a journey's fuel costs before the fare (`setCommute()`), and the drivers' fuel is struck after it (`motoring.setFuelBill()`). Inside statements that were already there, 0.7.43 has the food vouchers paid after the markets clear, 0.7.44 the strike settle the grocers' supplier credit, 0.7.46 Construction keep the materials its month drew as its books close (`Sector.beforeBank()`), 0.7.49 the treasury pay transit's bill beside the police's, 0.7.52 the anchor measure the lean against the Standard rule's advice at any strictness, and 0.7.54 the investors search for an order's size, its trim and a landlord's mortgage where they counted them a building at a time. One moved in 0.7.52: the twelfth month's autosave, from the top of the month, straight after the calendar turned, to its very end, after `recordMonth()`. 0.7.24 to 0.7.41, 0.7.45, 0.7.47, 0.7.48, 0.7.50, 0.7.51, 0.7.53 and 0.7.54 moved no statement: the generated list is the same with its line numbers stripped, bar two of 0.7.53's statements that now hold their counts as `long[]`. The edition before this one had the builders strike their crews before the posts are counted and migration handed the doors standing (0.7.17), each owner settle the escalation after the work and a business's tax back reach its till (0.7.19), and the demolitions close as the calendar turns, the overtime be read beside the site output and the hand on the queue be settled (0.7.22); the ones before it, the rollover and the fund's December share above the old first step (0.7.13, 0.7.14), the central bank's maturing par after the treasury settles (0.7.15), the bank's capital rule and prices at the top of the month and its provision and second look at the bottom (0.7.7, 0.7.8, 0.7.11, 0.7.12), and the resolution and the preferred after the shares trade (0.7.14).

> **Standing rule**
>
> A flow cannot be reconstructed from the state a month ended in. That is why the save carries income statements, the VAT ledger, the inventory baseline in units, wage history, loss streaks, plots consumed, the unburied backlog, last month's household shapes, the ring of the long sick, six months of prisoners, the railway's quote and what it carried, every sector's fleet and the memory of the commute, the treasury's journal for the month that ended and the one in progress, what the vault sold defending the currency, the bank's running costs and funding blend as it last priced them and the profit it booked after its close, a year of its month statements and of its balance sheets, its allowance and its worst year, every borrower's last quarter, the ledger of the surplus the rollover has netted, the four inputs the debt market's rate was struck from, the crews the builders kept on and the fill they were struck on, each order's contract on its site with the material its quote allowed for, the player's hand on the queue — the city's order of its own sites, the rushes and their months on overtime, the cancels waiting, the stopped shells, the demolitions and the buy-outs, with the overtime wages the next statement charges — the player's own decisions, migration's month and the dead by cause (0.7.27), what the railway was allowed to bill and what went abroad (0.7.29), the fund's ledger and the hand's orders (0.7.39), what people expect and how far they trust the bank (0.7.42), each household's last sale of groceries and the vouchers on it (0.7.43), what the grocers owe their suppliers (0.7.44), the month's trade in units, the
